page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a bare-metal server configuration within the General Purpose family, designed for high-concurrency enterprise workloads. The hardware is powered by dual-threaded Intel Xeon 6985P-C x86_64 processors running at 4.2 GHz, providing 144 physical cores and 288 dedicated vCPUs. The architecture features an extensive cache hierarchy comprising 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a unified 504 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic primitives.

System memory consists of 1080.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to roughly 3.75 GB of memory per vCPU. The server lacks bundled local storage and includes zero integrated GPUs. Bare-metal access eliminates hypervisor overhead, as reflected by the hypervisor flag being disabled while native hardware virtualization (VMX) remains available directly to the OS.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput across parallel tasks. The server scores 313,180.49 on stress-ng multi-core and 178,785.41 on the PassMark CPU suite, ranking in the top tier. Uncached memory bandwidth reaches 1087.82 GB/sec for large-block reads and 428.11 GB/sec for writes. The platform delivers top-tier performance in PassMark database operations (40,009.67) and Redis SET operations (413.48 million ops/sec), alongside multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 1589.0 GB/sec and static web serving throughput at 164.82 GB/sec. However, single-core metrics remain moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2302.79.

Given the absence of local disks, all persistent storage depends on network-attached solutions. The resource density provides substantial compute and memory efficiency for scale-up multi-threaded workloads, though CPU-based LLM token generation remains constrained compared to dedicated accelerators. The c4-standard-288-metal is well matched for in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching clusters, high-concurrency web serving tiers, and parallel batch processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288-metal is a high-density bare-metal server in the General Purpose family, powered by Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors delivering 144 physical cores and 288 dedicated vCPUs at 4.2 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture with 504 MB of L3 cache, it integrates AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets. The server includes 1080 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, offering high uncached read bandwidth exceeding 1087 GB/sec. It includes no integrated GPUs and provides no local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures. Synthetic benchmarks highlight top-tier multi-threaded compute and in-memory execution, achieving over 413 million Redis SET operations per second and high-throughput static web serving. While single-thread efficiency and CPU-only LLM generation remain average, the configuration is particularly capable for enterprise in-memory databases, dense caching deployments, compilation farms, and parallel batch analytics.
